item.title: 剑桥最年轻的黑人教授因大学调查抄袭指控而辞职
item.description:
伦敦（美联社）——一位英国社会学家因剑桥大学有史以来最年轻的黑人教授而闻名，在剑桥大学对有关他学历的“新信息”展开调查后，他辞职了。
杰森·阿尔戴教授于 2023 年成为剑桥大学教授，时年 37 岁。周三晚间，他在学术工作中被指控抄袭，并对有关他的运动和筹款成就的说法提出质疑，随后于周三晚间宣布了自己的决定。
“虽然批评是学术生活中不可避免的一部分，但我所经历的远远超出了学术分歧，”阿代在一份声明中说。“无情的指控、猜测和公众评论给我和我所爱的人造成了深远的影响。”
这份声明是由“好法律项目”发布的，该组织自上个月媒体批评阿代以来一直支持该组织。该组织早些时候散发的一封由两打学者和政界人士签署的信将抄袭指控描述为一场“诽谤运动”，旨在削弱阿尔代和其他拥有“影响力职位”的黑人。
阿代在剑桥大学的任命突显了他克服阅读障碍、发育迟缓和自闭症的个人故事，他说这些让他在 11 岁之前都不会说话，在十几岁之前都是文盲。阿代在下周出版的回忆录《伟大而不幸的事情》中讲述了他的故事。出版商西蒙与舒斯特周四发表声明称，将“按计划”发行这本书。
上个月，内森·科夫纳斯(Nathan Cofnas)公开提出了对其资格的质疑。内森·科夫纳斯曾是剑桥大学哲学研究员，在对多样性、公平和包容性项目的批评引发广泛抗议后离开了剑桥大学。
7月24日，伦敦《泰晤士报》发表了对Arday 2015年博士生的分析。论文强调了其所说的多个段落示例，这些段落与另一位研究人员早期撰写的论文“相同或接近相同”。
英国媒体还对阿代声称自己通过35天内跑30个马拉松、6天内跑600英里等壮举为慈善事业筹集了550万英镑（740万美元）的说法提出了质疑。
阿代告诉卫报新闻网站，这笔钱是在其他人的帮助下经过 20 年的时间筹集的。他说，保密协议阻止他透露其他人的名字。
剑桥大学最初支持阿代，称抄袭指控已由授予阿代博士学位的利物浦约翰摩尔斯大学进行了调查。
当剑桥周三展开调查时，情况发生了变化。
剑桥大学在一份声明中表示：“在获得有关阿戴教授的资格和荣誉任命的新信息后，剑桥大学已开始调查。”“为了确保公平的过程，在事情结束之前我们不会进一步发表评论。”
《伦敦泰晤士报》称，剑桥大学在提供新证据表明阿代的一些研究是“捏造”并包含“不可能”的证据后决定展开调查。
在上周发表的报纸采访中，阿代否认抄袭，但承认了一些错误，他说这些错误部分是由于他攻读博士学位时缺乏监督造成的。
阿代在辞职声明中继续为自己辩护，称他的决定“不应被解释为对学术失去信心”。
“也不应该被误认为是接受了我周围的叙述”，他说。“这只是一个人的决定，他已经达到了任何人应该合理承受的极限。”

item.title: 罗马尼亚紧急在多瑙河击沉4艘驳船，以维持核电站第二反应堆的运行
item.description:
罗马尼亚布加勒斯特（美联社）——罗马尼亚周四竞相将四艘满载岩石的驳船沉入多瑙河，试图将下游的水引向一座核电站，以便在其第二个反应堆可能因创纪录的低水位而被迫关闭之前争取更多时间。
该地区的极端热浪和少量降雨导致多瑙河在过去一周创下历史新低，迫使罗马尼亚切尔纳沃达核电站的反应堆上周关闭。全面运营后，这座国有核电站约占该国发电量的 20%，并使用河水来冷却反应堆。
这四艘驳船装载着罗马尼亚军方本周在多瑙河巴拉运河附近使用炸药从河中炸毁的岩石。一旦被淹没，驳船将形成一个水下屏障，将水引导到河流的主河道上并流向切尔纳沃达工厂。
该核电站主任罗密欧·乌尔扬 (Romeo Urjan) 周四在接受当地新闻频道 Digi24 采访时表示，从周三到周四，多瑙河的水位已下降了约两厘米（0.7 英寸），如果驳船不沉没，该核电站的第二个反应堆可能必须在五到六天内关闭。
“如果安装的驳船带来了多余的水……从今天开始，我们将讨论运行九到十天，而不是五到六天，”他说。
他补充说，驳船被淹没的影响可能需要大约一天的时间才能到达切尔纳沃达，因为它位于下游约 60 公里（37 英里）处。
自第一座反应堆关闭以来，当局实施了一系列紧急措施，包括疏浚河流。
本周，罗马尼亚多瑙河的水流量降至数十年来的最低水平，为每秒 1,400 立方米，还不到每年这个时候的正常水流量的三分之一。
代总理伊利·博洛扬7月31日宣布全国能源行业进入警戒状态。周四，他再次呼吁公民和地方当局自愿限制晚间高峰用电，并表示驳船的沉没可能会持续到周五。
博洛扬在一次政府会议后表示，迄今为止开展的工作旨在即使预计多瑙河水位较低，也能维持水流，重点是维持水流，以便第二个反应堆能够“以最大容量”运行。
他补充说，如果切尔纳沃达工厂完全关闭，罗马尼亚可能会面临潜在的能源短缺，并补充说，这可能取决于能否在晚间高峰时段从邻国进口能源，其中许多国家正在应对干旱期间的停工问题。
在邻国匈牙利，多瑙河的水位创历史新低，导致该国唯一的核电站几十年来首次陷入完全停电的边缘。在摩尔多瓦，该国严重依赖进口电力（包括来自罗马尼亚的电力），当局敦促公民自愿减少高峰时段的用电。
麦格拉斯从英国利明顿温泉报道。

item.title: 可能的霍尔木兹海峡协议、也门的大规模袭击和其他中东新闻
item.description:
Iran says it’s in the final stage of drafting an agreement on theStrait of Hormuzwaterway with Oman, while two Israeli soldiers have been killed in Lebanon.
Here’s a look at the latest developments in the Iran war and the wider Middle East on Thursday. Full coverage can be foundhere.
Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Esmail Baghaei, has saidan agreement on the Strait of Hormuz with Oman, which lies on the other side of the waterway, is in the “final stage” of drafting. Speaking Wednesday, he said a joint statement will be issued “if certain parties do not obstruct this process,” apparently referring to the U.S.
The agreement is likely to be contingent on the U.S. lifting its blockade on Iran’s ports.
A U.S. official who spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly said Thursday that any temporary routes through the Strait of Hormuz will not have impediments such as approvals, permissions, tolls or charges.
Asked Thursday if a deal has been reached with Iran to reopen the vital waterway, U.S. President Donald Trump said he didn’t want to say.
“It has been sort of open right now,” he told reporters in the Oval Office.
The strait is crucial to global shipping and energy supplies. Before the war, which began with U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran in February, about one-fifth of the world’s traded oil and natural gas passed through the waterway at the mouth of the Persian Gulf.
At least two ships were hit in the Strait of Hormuz in the past week, while several others reported near misses or warnings from entities claiming to represent Iran’s Revolutionary Guard, according to maritime data company Lloyd’s List Intelligence.
The company added that Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels continued to claim attacks on ships in the Red Sea. The claims could not be independently verified.
Vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz increased to 84 transits during the week of July 27 to Aug. 2, up from 45 the previous week. But traffic is still far below the more than 700 transits seen in a typical week before the crisis, Lloyd’s List said.
More than 10 civilians, including a 4-year-old child, were injured in Saudi Arabia on Thursday after a series of attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels, according to the Saudi military.
The attacks, which took place in the southern region of Najran, near the Yemeni border, came hours after the Iran-backed rebels claimed responsibility for another series of strikes in central and eastern Yemen that killed at least 30 government troops and wounded at least 50 others.
The back-to-back attacks mark a major escalation since a truce in 2022 largely halted fighting. The civil war pits the Iran-backed Houthis against a Saudi-led coalition allied with Yemen’s internationally recognized government.
A Houthi leader said Saudi-backed troops were targeted in the attacks and that “hundreds” were either killed or injured. The assaults hit camps for forces of the internationally recognized government in the provinces of Marib and Hadramout, the Yemeni officials said. They spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to the media.
Turki al-Malki, a spokesman for the Saudi military, said the later attack wounded seven Saudi nationals, one Yemeni, two Egyptians and one Pakistani expatriate. The Houthis did not release any statement.
Yemen has been embroiled in a civil war since 2014, when the Houthis seized the capital, Sanaa, and much of northern Yemen. The Saudi-led coalition intervened the following year.
— Samy Magdy in Cairo and Baraa Anwer in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
Two Israelisoldiers were killedand another four were seriously wounded in an explosion in southernLebanon, the Israeli military said Thursday. The deaths areIsrael’sfirst since a shaky truce was implemented in June between Israel and the Iran-backed Lebanese militant groupHezbollah.
The Israeli army launched strikes Wednesday in southern Lebanon in response to what it described as Hezbollah’s violation of the ceasefire and issued a call for residents of another village to flee — the first such warning Israel has issued in weeks.
The escalation came as Lebanese and Israeli negotiators met in Rome to discuss implementation of the June deal under which Israeli forces are supposed to withdraw from areas they occupy in southern Lebanon, in exchange for Hezbollah’s disarmament.
Ugandan authorities won parliamentary approval Thursdayto deploy troopsas part of the International Stabilization Force for Gaza.
The 20,000-strong force, proposed by U.S. President Donald Trump’s Board of Peace in February to ensure “future prosperity and enduring peace,”has not yet materialized.
Several other countries pledged troops to the mission, including Morocco, Kazakhstan, Kosovo, Albania and Indonesia, which has since put its commitment of troops on indefinite hold.
The Gaza ceasefire has stalled, as Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said this week thatIsrael will not withdrawfrom its current lines in Gaza until Hamas has completely disarmed.
Israeli prosecutors have charged a settler with the killing of a Palestinian community leader last year in the occupied West Bank.
Prosecutors accuse Yinon Levi of reckless manslaughter in the death of prominent Palestinian activist Awdah Hathaleen in July 2025. The charge holds a lesser punishment than murder under Israeli law. The indictment also charges Levi with armed trespassing and malicious property damage.
It is extremely rare for Israel to charge settlers with violence against Palestinians. Israeli rights group B’Tselem said the charges against Levi mark the first time since Hamas’ Oct. 7, 2023, attack that an Israeli has been indicted for the death of a Palestinian in the West Bank.
In that time, the group said, Israeli settlers and soldiers have killed at least 1,100 Palestinians in the territory.
Iraq said Thursday that any armed activity outside of state authority after Sept. 30 will be prosecuted under the country’s Anti-Terrorism Law, the latest move ina push to bring all weapons under government control.
Several powerful, Iran-backed armed factions have rejected calls to surrender weapons or dissolve their organizations, saying they remain committed to the “option of resistance.”
Saudi Arabia and the U.S. launched strikes on Iraq last week after Riyadh accused Iraqi militias of using drones to attack its oil facilities.
The retaliatory strikes in Iraq hit bases of the Popular Mobilization Forces, a collection of armed groups close to Iran that are officially part of Iraq’s security forces but often operate outside of state control.

item.title: 林赛·克兰西在谋杀案审判中哭泣，陪审员查看她最小孩子的尸检照片
item.description:
PLYMOUTH, Mass. (AP) —Lindsay Clancysobbed uncontrollably Thursday as jurors viewed autopsy photos of the youngest of her three children whom she strangled in 2023, until the court eventually had to take an unscheduled break.
In the second week of her Massachusetts murder trial, prosecutors brought more friends, a former work colleague and her former father-in-law to testify about Clancy’s mental and emotional state. They said she was mostly open about her postpregnancy mental health struggles but seemed like a loving mother who cared for her kids.
Clancy has pleaded not guilty to murder charges inthe deaths ofCora, 5, Dawson, 3, and 8-month-old Callan.
Defense attorneys don’t dispute that she killed her children on Jan. 24, 2023, after sending her husband out on errands, but they argue that she was too mentally ill to bear criminal responsibility for her actions.
Prosecutors, however, said thatsending her husband out of the house was a ruseand that the 35-year-old former labor and delivery nurse acted intentionally. She remains paralyzed from the waist down after jumping from the home’s second-story window that night.
EDITOR’S NOTE: This story includes discussion of suicide. If you or someone you know needs help, the national suicide and crisis lifeline in the U.S. is available by calling or texting 988.
Much of the week has been dominated by witnesses detailing their memories of Clancy in the days, weeks and months before the killings.
Outwardly, Clancy appeared normal, most said, attending family functions, lunches with friends and activities with her children. None of the witnesses Thursday testified they heard Clancy express suicidal or homicidal thoughts, talking of hearing voices or wanting to harm her children.
But after the birth of her third child, she told a friend she was having trouble sleeping and noted harmful side effects from medications she was taking. Another former colleague at Massachusetts General Hospital, Andrea Hennigan, recalled a lunch where Clancy said she wouldn’t return to work because she “was not in a mental state to take care of patients.”
“She talked about insomnia and not feeling herself,” she said. “I believe she might have used the words brain fog or something like that.”
The month of the killings, Clancy texted Hennigan that she was experiencing “bad or negative side effects” from her medications. She told another witness, Amy Bevins, around then that the medications had “caused her to have some dark thoughts.”
Another witness, Bethany Decollibus, attended a birthday party for Clancy’s daughter, Cora, in January 2023. Asked about her sleep troubles, Clancy said “things haven’t gotten better and that she feels like a zombie.”
Christopher Clancy praised his former daughter-in-law’s mothering skills. But he admitted knowing she was having issues. At one point, he suggested the grandchildren stay with him and his wife, but his son declined.
“I knew she was having a hard time sleeping,” Christopher Clancy said. “I knew she just didn’t feel well. I knew she went to the emergency room where my wife was working. Those types of struggles.”
Lindsay Clancy’s attorneys in criminal and civil cases have said that she hadpostpartum psychosis, a condition that a small fraction of women exhibit after childbirth, and that she had bipolar disorder that wasn’t fully diagnosed until after the killings. Her attorneys say her condition seemed to worsen on the psychiatric medications, some of them problematic for bipolar patients.
If convicted of murder, she faces life in prison without parole. If found not guilty due to a lack of criminal responsibility, she would be committed to a state mental health facility.
Meanwhile, the judge and the district attorney learned Thursday that they face a retrial in another case involving a mother’s mental state when she killed her two school-age children in 2018.
Massachusetts’ top court threw out Latarsha Sanders’murder convictionsin thestabbingsof sons Edson “Marlon” Brito, 8, and La’son Brito, 5.
Sanders told police in a recorded interview that she stabbed the boys because “bad people” text-messaged her commands to carry out a “ritual” connected to “Voodoo stuff” andthe Illuminati. The latter is a purported powerful secret society at the center of various conspiracy theories, and Sanders’ family said she had become obsessively fearful of it.
Like Clancy’s lawyers, Sanders’ defense argued she was mentally ill and shouldn’t be held criminally responsible, while prosecutors said she acted deliberately.
A defense neuropsychologist diagnosed Sanders with schizophrenia spectrum disorder, among other conditions, and testified that she was “grossly psychotic” when she killed the children.
The Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court faulted the judge for not letting jurors hear many specifics from Sanders’ medical records. They showed, among other things, that clinicians at a prison and a psychiatric hospital suggested similar diagnoses after Sanders’ arrest.
Withholding the records from jurors “impermissibly stripped” the defense of its medical foundation, Justice Frank M. Gaziano wrote in a unanimous decision.
Plymouth County District Attorney Timothy Cruz’s office said in a statement that it was thinking through next steps. Messages seeking comment were sent to a clerk for Superior Court Justice William Sullivan and to a court system spokesperson.
Sanders’ lawyer, Robert F. Shaw Jr., said he looked forward to retrying the case.
“The hope is that those records and that evidence will be able to be viewed by a jury with fresh eyes,” he said by phone.

item.title: 华盛顿斯波坎被控纵火的男子告诉警方，他计划了数周的野火
item.description:
警方称，一名被控在华盛顿州斯波坎点燃野火的男子策划了数周的犯罪活动，并研究了何时最适合点燃野火，这场野火已摧毁了数百座建筑物。
亚伦·法里纳奇 (Aaron Farinacci) 被捕后接受采访时表示，“火是强大的、美丽的，经历过火的东西会经历一种重生，”斯波坎县警探迈克尔·德拉普 (Michael Drapeau) 在周三的一份法庭文件中写道。
37 岁的法里纳奇被指控引发了 Old Trails 火灾，这是斯波坎地区的三场大火之一，已烧毁了 850 多座建筑物，摧毁了整个社区和街道。数万人被迫撤离，许多人仍然无法回家。目前尚无死亡或重伤报告。
Farinacci 还因与 2025 年夏季和上个月发生的四起较小火灾有关而受到指控。
他原定于周四因五项一级纵火罪被提审，但他的律师要求在他提出抗辩之前进行能力评估。斯波坎高等法院法官杰里米·施密特表示，他将审查该请求。他设定了 200 万美元的保释金，裁定法里纳奇对社区安全构成风险、潜逃风险，并且有可能发生暴力犯罪。
辩护律师科林·夏博诺没有立即回复寻求置评的消息。
侦探写道，当警方最初联系法里纳奇时，他否认点燃了旧道火灾，但在接受德拉波采访时，他承认去年和上个月发生了那场火灾以及其他火灾。这导致了另外四项纵火指控。
他告诉侦探，他总是携带大麻或香烟，因此他有正当理由拥有打火机和火柴。
“他知道，只要有时间，纵火是一种很容易逃脱的犯罪，他也有时间，”德拉波说。
德拉波说，法里纳奇研究了天气，预测哪一天会炎热、多风、湿度低，从而引发老道火灾。侦探说，他还查阅了一位著名连环纵火犯的作品，并购买了一些物品，用笔记本纸、火柴、香烟和橡皮筋制作了一个“延时装置”，用于点燃野火。
侦探说，法里纳奇选择 8 月 1 日星期六起火，因为他知道会有强风，风速将达到 50 英里/小时（80 公里/小时）。
德雷波说，法里纳奇说，他知道情况会变得很糟，但声称他不打算让它增长得那么快。
斯波坎县警长约翰·诺尔斯周四表示，人们需要几周时间才能安全返回斯波坎大火烧毁地区的家园。调查人员表示，另外两起重大火灾，即秋巷火灾和费尔维尤火灾，也是由人引发的，尽管不一定是故意的。
64 岁的保罗·柴尔德 (Paul Child) 被认为是带领警察找到法里纳奇的人。当他和孙子沿着铁轨行驶时，他看到一个男人站在那里，看着附近的树木。大约10分钟后，该男子还在那里。
“他在灌木丛中弯腰，表现得很紧张，”柴尔德周二告诉美联社。“你能感觉到这家伙在搞事情。”
德拉波表示，法里纳奇还承认对 2025 年夏季他的公寓楼附近发生的 25 起火灾负责。大多数火灾发生在斯波坎河或百年步道附近。
法庭文件称，法里纳奇承认于 2025 年 7 月 6 日在百年步道附近点燃了奥布里·怀特大火，并威胁到了房屋和建筑物。这导致了疏散和道路封闭。调查确定这是纵火所致，但警方当时没有任何嫌疑人。
法里纳奇还因2025年7月8日开始的米纳赫火灾、2025年8月11日发生的乔治堡火灾和2026年7月24日发生的印第安布拉夫火灾而面临纵火指控。
2010 年，法里纳奇在亚利桑那州梅萨杀死了父亲，之后在监狱里服刑了大约十年。他还开枪自杀。他被指控犯有谋杀罪，但在 2012 年承认过失杀人和严重袭击罪。法里纳奇的律师在案件审理过程中多次对他的心理健康状况表示担忧。
德拉波表示，法里纳奇表示，他于 2022 年 10 月搬到了斯波坎地区的库珀河公寓 (Copper River Apartments)。
侦探称，Farinacci 的儿子出生于 2025 年，他开始难以处理“生活问题”，并开始吸食大麻。
美联社记者哈莉·戈尔登（Hallie Golden）在西雅图对这篇报道做出了贡献。

item.title: 参议院委员会投票判定福奇藐视法庭拒绝回答新冠问题
item.description:
WASHINGTON (AP) — A Senate committee voted along party lines Thursday tohold Dr. Anthony Fauci in contempt of Congressover his refusal to answer questions at a hearing on his handling of the COVID-19 pandemic, setting up a referral to the Justice Department for potential investigation over whether the country’s longtime topinfectious disease officialproperly exercised his constitutional rights.
A department spokesperson confirmed Thursday evening that the department had received the contempt referral, is “reviewing it and will work with the Senate accordingly.”
The vote approving the contempt resolution came a weekafter Fauci invoked his Fifth Amendment rightagainst self-incrimination more than 100 times when he appeared before the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, an episode that raised fresh legal questions about the ability of Congress to compel testimony from a previously pardoned witness.
Republican Sen. Rand Paul of Kentucky, the committee chairman who pressed for the contempt finding, said that constitutional protection did not apply becauseFauci last year received a pardon from Democratic President Joe Bidenand thus did not have to worry about the threat of prosecution.
“Dr. Fauci faced no risk of federal prosecution,” Paul said at the outset of Thursday’s vote. “All he had to do was tell the truth.”
AP’s Lisa Dwyer reports a Senate committee voted to hold Fauci in contempt of Congress.
He told colleagues that the issue before them was not Fauci’s opinions, policies or “anything he said from a podium six years ago.”
Instead, he added, “We were voting on whether a witness who has received the benefit of a sweeping federal pardon can be ordered by this committee to answer questions and then defy that order without consequence.”
Fauci, in a statement last week explaining his decision to invoke his Fifth Amendment rights, said he had good reason to fear the possibility of criminal charges given what he said was Paul’s determination “to get me to say something, anything, that could vindicate his repeated public pledges that I end up, in his words, quote, behind bars, unquote.”
Fauci’s lawyer, David Schertler, said in a statement that the contempt resolution was “a continuation of Senator Paul’s personal vendetta against Dr. Fauci, who spent 50 years in public health and has saved countless lives.” Schertler accused Paul of abusing his power by trying to “weaponize the Justice Department.”
“Today’s partisan committee vote is a crude political stunt intended to punish Dr. Fauci for exercising his constitutional rights,” Schertler said. “The Senate should reject Senator Paul’s meritless and politically-motivated contempt resolution. For years, Senator Paul has proclaimed to anyone who would listen that Dr. Fauci should be prosecuted and put in prison. Dr. Fauci has committed no crime – and Senator Paul knows it.”
The pardon from Biden covered acts from 2014 through the January 2025 day it was issued, but does not shield him from state-level prosecutions or protect him from federal investigations into any testimony he did give that lawmakers deemed false. The current Justice Department hasrepeatedly initiated false statement investigations into perceived adversaries of President Donald Trumpas part of what critics have called a retribution campaign.
Democrats who unanimously opposed the contempt resolution agreed with Fauci that he had a well-founded fear of self-incrimination given the publicly stated desires of Republican lawmakers, including Paul, to see him prosecuted in connection with COVID.The Trump administration has also raised questions about whether the Biden pardons were validgiven Biden’s frequent use of an autopen to conduct official business.
“The goal was to wait for Dr. Fauci to make any kind of misstatement and then have a weaponized Department of Justice file criminal charges for that new statement that would not have been covered by the pardon, leaving Dr. Fauci little choice but to invoke his constitutional right to not walk directly into a trap,” said Sen. Maggie Hassan, D-N.H., before the vote.
Trump himself weighed in Thursday at the White House, noting in response to a reporter’s question that two advisers from his first term,Steve BannonandPeter Navarro, were jailed on contempt charges during the Biden administration after they defied congressional subpoenas and refused to even show up for their scheduled hearings.
“When you see that happen, you sort of say maybe he should,” Trump said of Fauci being prosecuted. “What he did is far more serious than a lot of crimes, frankly.”
Paul’s decision to send the referral directly to the Justice Department would leave it to prosecutors in Washington to decide whether to investigate or potentially attempt to prosecute Fauci for contempt. A referral from Congress does not compel the Justice Department to act.
The committee’s top Democrat, Sen. Gary Peters of Michigan, questioned whether the referral would be legally valid if Paul did not seek a vote before the full Senate, where the 60 votes needed to pass the resolution are seen as unlikely. He said punishing a witness for exercising a constitutional right against self-incrimination would complicate future efforts by Congress to conduct oversight and compel appearances and testimony.
“If this committee now seeks to punish a witness for asserting their (constitutionally) protected Fifth Amendment rights, future witnesses will argue that appearing before Congress exposes them to punishment regardless of whether they comply with a subpoena and invoke a constitutional protection,” he said. “They will point directly to this vote — this vote — as a justification for refusing to appear at all.”

item.title: 特朗普的印地赛车比赛：在时速 25 英里的区域以井盖位移扭矩完成 200 英里
item.description:
WASHINGTON (AP) — The speed limit along Pennsylvania Avenue is 25 mph.
But the open-wheel race cars roaring through the longest straightaway of the upcoming WashingtonIndyCar raceorganized by PresidentDonald Trumpcould be going nearly eight times that fast.
“If we did that during the regular day, I think people would be put in jail, perhaps for the rest of their lives,” Trump joked recently while hosting an IndyCar pit crew at the White House to hype the Freedom 250 Grand Prix.
The race, scheduled for Aug. 22 and 23, features vehicles that typically reach street-course speeds approaching 200 mph and have enough torque to tear off manhole covers. It is the latest — and the fastest — of the major events Trump has hosted against the backdrop of America’s 250th birthday, a larger celebration he hasmade as much about himself as possible.
The president staged aUFC fighton the White House’sSouth Lawnfor his 80th birthday in June and held a rally to kick off the Great American State Fair on the National Mall aftermost of the event’s scheduled musical acts pulled out. He headlined another rally for July Fourth on the National Mall, ahead of a massive fireworks display marking the semiquincentennial of the Declaration of Independence’s signing.
Historian Michael D. Hattem said Trump’s events have put little focus on “addressing the specific history of the founding of the country or the 250th.” White House spokesman Davis Ingle countered that Trump “is focused on saving our country — not garnering recognition.”
Trump is “ensuring that America gets the spectacular 250th birthday it deserves,” Ingle said in a statement, adding that the series of events Trump has helped organize shows that “2026 is sparking a renewal of patriotism and national pride” under the president’s leadership.
The IndyCar event will be 250 miles (400 kilometers) over 147 laps on a 1.66-mile (2.67-kilometer) track featuring seven turns. Series owner Roger Penske, whom Trumpawarded the Presidential Medal of Freedomin 2019, led the effort to make the race happen in the District of Columbia. He gave the president a racing helmet, urging him to wear it “when you’re riding around in The Beast, leading the field to the green flag” — a traditional prerace kickoff that may feature the presidential limo.
D.C. Mayor Muriel Bowser suggested that the event was the “first, to be followed by second and third,” and Trump says he’d like more Washington races in future years. But Bud Denker, president of Penske Corporation and the race’s chair, isn’t committing.
“It is the first ever,” he said. “It might be the only.”
Denker said Penske is paying for the “vast majority” of the race, including road construction and improvements, while the city handles some “very limited” repaving. The District of Columbia referred questions about repaving costs to Penske.
About a third of the track needs road improvement, a cost that should come in at under $3 million, Denker said. That’s less than is often spent on road fixes ahead of other races, including in Markham, Ontario, where up to $9 million is being doled out on improvements for the IndyCar race being held the week before Washington’s event, he said.
“The roads here are in pretty good shape,” Denker said, noting that area residents are surprised when they hear him say that.
But that reflects the nature of the nation’s capital: The stretch of Pennsylvania Avenue from the White House to the U.S. Capitol is repaved every four years for presidential inaugurations. Another key area along Constitution Avenue was resurfaced aftertanks rolled down itfor Trump’smilitary parade marking July 4 last year.
One issue, Denker said, is the 220-plus manhole covers on the race circuit that had to be welded to ensure the race cars don’t suck them off the road. About 50 of those need to be fitted with silicone because they are set too deep into the road, creating a bump, he said.
Organizers also are paying to build 1,800 walls weighing 10,000 pounds (4,536 kilograms) each to ring the track and metal detectors that will be manned by the Secret Service.
Penske is relying on the federal departments of Interior and Transportation, Denker said, not for funding but for help with issues such as permitting, allowing Chevrolet to set up a car display and vendors to sell merchandise and beer on the National Mall — activities that aren’t normally allowed.
The race will go in the rain, except in the event of lightning or if major puddling makes the track slippery. Denker said that 288,000 free tickets were requested through a lottery system — exceeding the 130,000 spectators whom organizers plan to host on each of the event’s two days.
“It’s just going to be something we’ve never seen before,” said Denker, who said there will be 90 minutes of prerace show that Sunday and military flyovers like those that thundered over the National Mall for July 4.
Bob Varsha, a veteran sports announcer who long specialized in motorsports, said that a track running less than 1.7 miles (2.7 kilometers) is shorter than most street race courses and that Washington’s design may feature 90-degree corners. That means cars likely won’t be able to maintain top speeds. “It’s going to be a lot of speed up, slow down,” he said.
“It’s a huge idea,” Varsha said. “And I hope it goes as well as it possibly can.”
The track heads down Pennsylvania Avenue from 3rd Street to 9th Street NW, then doubles back to 7th Street, then goes south to Independence Avenue alongside the National Mall before looping back to 3rd Street.
Turn 1 has the U.S. Capitol’s west façade as its backdrop, while the pit lane is on the straightaway between Turn 1 and Turn 2, along Pennsylvania Avenue. Other sections feature views of the Washington Monument and the Smithsonian’s National Air & Space Museum.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Washington hasn’t seen a race like this since Thomas Jefferson helped mark America’s 25th birthday on July 4, 1801.
That’s when the north grounds of President’s Park were thronged with booths, and attending crowds watched horse racing and cockfighting, according to the White House Historical Association. Jefferson eventually opened the White House and “invited everyone in to partake of his hospitality,” with ordinary people joining military officers and visiting Cherokee chiefs inside, the association said.
But Hattem, who has written extensively on how the U.S. has celebrated its independence, said that, the association’s account aside, contemporary descriptions of that celebration didn’t mention horse racing. He also said that Washington then was a sparsely populated swamp with the White House but very little actual city, meaning there wasn’t much infrastructure for such races.
Instead, Hattem said, accounts from 1801 focused on how Jefferson — the first president from the Democratic-Republican Party — handled July 4 celebrations differently than his predecessors, George Washington and John Adams, who favored the Federalist Party’s backing of a strong central government and close ties to Great Britain.
Jefferson’s festivities were more utilitarian and, according to the National Intelligencer newspaper, offered “no ostentatious homage to power.”
“That is a strong contrast between then and the present,” Hattem said.

item.title: 因凡蒂诺危机会议后，欧足联维持抵制世界杯的威胁
item.description:
尽管国际足联为其出售世界杯股份的失败计划道歉，但欧洲足球管理机构仍保留抵制国际足联比赛的威胁。
欧足联周四重申，它对国际足联主席詹尼·因凡蒂诺失去了信心，并表示撤销抵制威胁的条件尚未满足。
欧足联在一份声明中表示：“欧足联各协会对于不参加国际足联比赛的附加条件非常明确。”“首先，必须撤回出售主要赛事的提议，其次，必须保证永远不会再进行此类破坏比赛的尝试。
“这些条件尚未得到满足。此外，欧足联在周六的声明中明确表示，它对詹尼·因凡蒂诺的主席职位失去了信心。这一立场保持不变。”
对于因凡蒂诺来说，这又是一个痛苦的一天，全球足球运动员联盟 FIFPRO 指责他“严重滥用总统权力”。
英格兰足协也撤回了对因凡蒂诺连任的支持。
就连国际特赦组织也表示，“当前的危机凸显了治理改革的必要性。”
周三在摩洛哥举行的高层峰会后，国际足联和因凡蒂诺试图建立统一战线，当时峰会宣布主席得到了出席会议的高层工作人员的全力支持。
该世界管理机构还就其通过商业子公司在世界杯期间出售利润而引发争议的错误表示歉意，并承诺“确保此类情况不再发生”。
国际足联表示，因凡蒂诺现已放弃的项目引发了广泛谴责，引发了动荡，希望这次会议能够“帮助恢复对该组织的信心”。
欧足联投票决定，如果国际足联比赛继续进行，将放弃该赛事。即使在因凡蒂诺仓促改变方针之后，欧洲管理机构仍表示对国际足联的领导失去了信心，这为挑战他的主席职位铺平了道路。
欧足联在其挑衅声明中明确表示其立场仍然不变。
“昨天宣布国际足联主席雇用的一些人（他们的职业生涯取决于他的青睐）同意他的观点，但这并没有改变任何事情，”它说。
詹姆斯·罗布森 (James Robson) 位于 https://x.com/jamesalanrobson

item.title: 高夫支持 WTA 基因测试，同时批评它如何造成对跨性别群体的敌意
item.description:
多伦多（美联社）——可可·高夫了解 WTA 巡回赛新推出的基因测试政策背后的原因。这位两届大满贯冠军不喜欢的是，这种讨论变得政治化，产生了高夫所说的“对跨性别群体的敌意”。
对她来说，这个话题需要更细致的对话，这就是为什么高芙在周三首场比赛战胜凯拉·戴之后在多伦多举行的加拿大公开赛上接受记者采访时提供了她所谓的细致入微的答案。
“所以，是的，我想我有点同意努力保护女子体育的公平性。但我也不喜欢它所造成的攻击，”高夫说。“那些人并不真正关心，只是想以此作为攻击跨性别群体的理由——所以我也不太喜欢这样做。”
她的评论是针对女子网球协会上个月对所有运动员引入一次性强制性基因测试作为参加 2028 年洛杉矶奥运会的要求的回应。
玩家正在接受 SRY 基因测试，这是通常在 Y 染色体上发现的 DNA 片段，它启动子宫内的男性性别发育并表明睾丸的存在。
目前尚不清楚有多少（如果有的话）跨性别女性参加奥运会级别的比赛，更不用说 WTA 巡回赛了。
WTA表示，该政策区分了生物性别和性别认同，并且“无意不尊重或质疑任何人的性别认同或尊严”。
田径、滑雪和拳击运动管理机构已经实施的强制性性别筛查遭到了人权专家和活动团体的批评。
高夫质疑该流程的引入是否可以更加透明，他指出一些参与者只是在新政策宣布时才知道这一点。

item.title: 凯特琳·克拉克、安吉尔·里斯、佩奇·布克斯将首次亮相世界杯，美国男篮迎来新纪元
item.description:
纽约（美联社）——凯特琳·克拉克、安吉尔·里斯和佩奇·布克斯将于下个月作为美国女足国家队队员首次亮相世界杯。
这三人将努力帮助美国队连续第五次夺得国际篮联世界杯冠军。与这些年轻明星一起参加的还有奥运会奖牌获得者阿贾·威尔逊 (A’ja Wilson)、布里安娜·斯图尔特 (Breanna Stewart)、纳菲萨·科利尔 (Napheesa Collier)、切尔西·格雷 (Chelsea Gray)、杰基·杨 (Jackie Young)、卡利亚·科珀 (Kahleah Copper) 和凯尔西·普拉姆 (Kelsey Plum)。
“当你争夺金牌时总是好的，这是一个巨大的荣誉，”四届 WNBA MVP 威尔逊说。“这是我不会掉以轻心的事情。是时候去那里享受一些乐趣并赢得胜利了。”
莱恩·霍华德和阿利亚·波士顿也将在世界杯上首次亮相，以使球队更加完善。
美国篮球国家队总经理苏·伯德表示：“我很高兴宣布 2026 年美国篮球女子国家队名单。”“这是一支非常有才华的团队，他们赢得了参加柏林比赛的机会。穿着美国队球衣是一种荣幸，我知道这 12 名球员将在我们追逐另一枚金牌时承担起这一责任。我迫不及待地想看看这支球队共同取得的成就。”
这是美国男篮首次由总经理选择球队。过去是一个委员会。卡拉劳森将担任球队教练。
斯图尔特是美国篮球历史上第三位参加过四次世界杯比赛的球员，此前伯德参加了五次世界杯，戴安娜·陶拉西也参加了四次世界杯。
美国队将在9月4日至13日在柏林举行的世界杯上与中国队、意大利队和捷克队进行撞球比赛。WNBA 将在赛季中休息近三周以适应这一赛事。
克拉克、布克斯和里斯帮助美国队赢得了在波多黎各举行的世界杯预选赛。
萨布丽娜·伊内斯库（Sabrina Ionescu）过去几年一直是美国队名单中的重要组成部分，但本赛季被排除在外。
伯德说，她给这次没有入选球队的许多球员打了电话，其中包括伊内斯库。
“我认为我们都同意最困难的部分，这是我永远不会交易的问题，是我们有这么多的天赋，”伯德说。“这样做的美妙之处在于，这意味着几乎所有球员都想加入这支球队，愿意加入这支球队。这是一种牺牲。这是一种时间承诺。”
阿莉莎·托马斯帮助美国队在巴黎奥运会上赢得金牌，但此后没有参加任何美国篮球训练营。明尼苏达州新秀奥利维亚·迈尔斯也没有参加过任何美国训练营。
“伟大的球员。观看比赛非常有趣，”伯德谈到迈尔斯时说道，迈尔斯是 WNBA 年度最佳新秀的领跑者。“看着她在这个联盟中成长真是太棒了……她以前曾在美国篮球队效力过。毫无疑问，她将来会成为球队的一员。”
美联社WNBA：https://apnews.com/hub/wnba-basketball

item.title: 约翰·卡彭特将地狱电梯的梦想变成了“大教堂”图画小说和专辑
item.description:
洛杉矶（美联社）——约翰·卡彭特在他的职业生涯中经常与他最亲近的人合作。但制作《大教堂》这本图画小说以及周五发行的原创专辑确实是一件家庭事务。
这位曾拍摄过《怪形》和《万圣节》等开创性恐怖电影的著名导演表示，如今的电影业都是“企业化”的。因此，这位 78 岁的老人更喜欢寻找更便宜的替代方法来保持创造性的满足。
卡彭特也是一位多产的作曲家，他梦见了洛杉矶市中心一座废弃的教堂，里面有一部通往地狱的电梯，之后他邀请他的教子丹尼尔·戴维斯和儿子科迪合作制作这张专辑。它由令人毛骨悚然的器乐曲目组成，让人想起他的一些标志性经典作品，比如《万圣节》的主题曲。然后，他向漫画出版商妻子桑迪·金寻求漫画小说方面的帮助。
卡彭特、他的儿子和戴维斯向美联社讲述了他们的艺术创作过程、对人工智能的担忧以及对波士顿凯尔特人队伟大拉里·伯德的噩梦。为了清晰和简洁，采访经过编辑。
约翰·卡普特：我想，我以前是一名职业电影导演，这张专辑对于电影来说会是一个很棒的配乐。不过，这部电影要耗资数亿美元，为什么不拍一部图画小说呢？我的妻子拥有一家漫画书公司，所以让我们写小说并为其绘制插图，然后我们就可以对其进行评分。
约翰·卡普特：不，相反。我导演这部电影，按照我想要的方式剪辑，然后看音乐。所以，音乐只是功能性的。它支持故事和人物等等。
自从我全职从事电影行业以来，电影业发生了变化。现在都是公司了。我来自学生电影制作，我们没有钱，所以我们无法聘请作曲家。我必须自己做。但现在我有这些流浪汉和我一起做，所以我不必那么努力工作。
约翰·卡普特：从来没有。这是第一次。我的大多数梦想都非常相似，而且它们不是为电影而制作的。它们总是关于我在城市中迷路并试图找到回家的路，但街道在我身上发生了变化，我找不到回家的路。或者我正在寻找电影院区，当我到达那里时，它们都关门了。
科迪·卡普特：从大学起我就一直在写梦想日记。我有这些精神病的梦。我只是想记住他们，你知道吗？
约翰·卡普特：篮球梦想？你没看到有人开始运球吗？
科迪·卡普特：是拉里·伯德。但事实证明他已经死了，而我正在和他的鬼魂互动。
约翰·卡普特：嗯，人们告诉我这很危险。我不知道——这是什么意思？这是否意味着它开始自行学习？
戴维斯：我们喜欢创作音乐。我希望它能够帮助完成更多任务类的事情，例如预测新曲目并了解我的工作流程。但我们喜欢创造东西，那么我们为什么要使用它呢？
科迪·卡彭特：我不知道。我认识一个经常做人工智能音乐的人，他把他做的所有这些东西都发给我，我的意思是，我认为在某个时候我们将不再有工作了。我真的觉得这太神奇了，它的进展速度有多快。但我不知道。没有人知道。
约翰·卡普特：我认为音乐是最伟大的艺术形式。我讨厌这么说。但它不需要任何东西。我们都可以在不同的国家听到它。美妙的音乐让我们感动。你是说机器可以做到这一点？我不相信。这让我很烦恼。这是人的事。我希望它来自我们。我真的这么做。
约翰·卡普特：为什么你刚刚看到它？
约翰·卡普特：我很高兴你喜欢它。我几乎对我拍的每一部电影都很满意。
约翰·卡普特：我不会告诉你。

item.title: 家乐氏表示，将在今年年底前去除谷物中的人工染料
item.description:
WK 家乐氏 (WK Kellogg) 周四表示，将在今年年底之前从其所有谷物食品中去除人工色素。
这一变化比原计划提前了一年。家乐氏去年 8 月表示，将在 2027 年底前去除谷物中的合成染料。
但该公司周四表示，它已经找到了基于水果和蔬菜的果汁，可以为 Froot Loops 和 Apple Jacks 等谷物赋予独特的颜色。这家总部位于密歇根州巴特尔克里克的公司表示，它还投资了设备，使其能够过渡到自然色。
该公司表示，它还将从少数仍含有 BHT（一种人工防腐剂）的谷物中去除。
家乐氏首席增长官 Doug VanDeVelde 在一份声明中表示：“越来越多的消费者正在寻找由简单、可识别的成分制成的食品，我们很自豪能够比计划更早地满足这些期望。”
家乐氏多年来一直面临着要求从谷物中去除人工成分的压力，该公司已经在加拿大等其他国家这样做了。2024 年，数十人在家乐氏总部外集会，提交了有 40 万个签名的请愿书，要求该公司去除人造染料和 BHT。
在唐纳德·特朗普总统的卫生部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪的领导下，这种压力越来越大，他敦促食品公司逐步淘汰基于石油的人造染料。去年 8 月，家乐氏还与德克萨斯州总检察长肯·帕克斯顿签署了一项协议，称将在 2027 年底前“永久去除谷物中的有毒染料”。
零售商也迫使企业采取行动。今年早些时候，塔吉特表示将在 5 月底之前停止销售含有人工色素的谷物食品。沃尔玛也表示将在 2027 年 1 月之前从其商店品牌中去除人工色素。

item.title: 随着油价上涨和更多财报发布，美国股市小幅走低
item.description:
纽约（美联社）——周四，由于华尔街面临油价上涨和公司盈利好坏参半的压力，股市进一步远离近期纪录。
华尔街本周开盘飙升并创下历史新高，但在过去两天里已经平静下来。市场正在应对美国与伊朗持续战争及其对通胀影响的不确定性。来自各个行业的公司报告了最新的财务业绩，为本已繁忙的一轮企业盈利增添了色彩。
标准普尔 500 指数下跌 13.59 点，跌幅 0.2%，至 7,709.96 点。尽管该指数仍有望实现每周上涨，但该指数距离周二创下的纪录进一步拉开。
道琼斯工业平均指数下跌 464.02 点，跌幅 0.9%，至 53,885.10 点。纳斯达克综合指数下跌 15.09 点，跌幅 0.1%，至 26,348.35 点。
道琼斯指数和纳斯达克指数也将在周五迎来每周稳健的上涨。
Bellwether Wealth 总裁兼首席投资官克拉克·贝林 (Clark Bellin) 在一份研究报告中表示：“8 月的开局非常强劲，但八月还有很长的路要走，而且八月通常是股市波动的月份。”
华纳兄弟探索公司 (Warner Bros. Discovery) 公布的盈利超出投资者预期，股价上涨 1.7%。Molson Coors 也公布了令人鼓舞的财务业绩，股价上涨 1.3%。
霍尼韦尔航空航天公司 (Honeywell Aerospace) 的业绩远低于预期，股价下跌 23.2%。数字广告公司 AppLovin 公布最近一个季度的财务业绩好坏参半，股价下跌 19.7%。
公司强劲的整体利润有助于缓解华尔街对市场定价过高的担忧。标准普尔 500 指数成分股中约 85% 的公司已公布业绩，该时期的整体盈利增长有望达到 2021 年以来最强劲的水平。
除盈利外，SpaceX 上涨 6.1%。随着股票禁售期到期，早期投资者和员工持有的超过 9.11 亿股 SpaceX 股票周四有资格出售。这是埃隆·马斯克公司首次公开募股期间最初向公众出售的股票的两倍多。SpaceX 在 6 月份上市后股价一度飙升至每股 225 美元，但此后已跌破其最初的 135 美元发行价。该股目前交易价格约为 115 美元。
由于美国与伊朗的战争抑制了全球石油流动，不确定性仍然存在，油价上涨。国际标准布伦特原油价格上涨 3.8%，至 82.49 美元。
伊朗表示，它即将与阿曼就重新开放霍尔木兹海峡达成协议。唐纳德·特朗普总统此前也曾表示，协议已接近达成，但在过去五个月里，冲突发生了多次。
世界上五分之一的石油和天然气贸易曾经经过霍尔木兹海峡。冲突期间，油价飙升至 113 美元，油价上涨导致汽油价格和运输成本上升，加剧了通货膨胀。
通货膨胀率停留在 3% 以上，成本上升一直在挤压企业和家庭，同时有可能抑制更广泛的经济增长。美国经济第二季度缓慢增长 1.5%。家庭仍在支出，就业市场依然富有弹性，但这两个经济领域的担忧依然存在。
天然气价格上涨和运输货物成本增加可能会促使家庭将更多支出转向必需品。这可能会损害专注于为许多人提供非必需品和服务（例如旅行和娱乐）的企业。
就业依然强劲，但增长一直在放缓。周四的每周报告显示，上周申请失业救济的美国人人数有所增加，但裁员人数仍处于过去几年的历史健康范围内。6 月份雇主减少了招聘，仅增加了 57,000 个工作岗位。最新的七月份月度就业报告将于周五发布。
对通胀和就业市场的担忧促使美联储维持基准利率稳定。不过，顽固的通胀正促使央行在年底前加息，以帮助抑制通胀。加息还可能减缓经济增长，同时打压股票和其他投资的价格。
债券市场国债收益率上升。周三晚间，10 年期国债收益率从 4.63% 升至 4.67%。
美联社撰稿人伊莱恩·库尔滕巴赫 (Elaine Kurtenbach) 和亨金·金 (Hyung-jin Kim) 对本报告做出了贡献。

item.title: 在大流行后的世界中，求职者感觉夹在西装和连帽衫之间
item.description:
NEW YORK (AP) — The matching blazer and pants Dani McEwen wore to a job interview at an insurance company felt like a smart choice, until she noticed most of the employees had on T-shirts and jeans.
“The first thing that went through my mind was that I probably looked like I was trying way too hard and maybe seemed too uptight,” McEwen, a student at Baldwin Wallace University in Berea, Ohio, said.
With virtual interviews and casualwork environmentsproliferating, job candidates are having a hard time figuring out what to wear when they meetpotential employersonline or in person. Polished suits and other types of professional business attire — the typical recommendation of career advisers in years past — no longer are the default option when interviewers may show up in hoodies and shorts.
The disconnect between long-established conventions and the less-rigid workplace settings of apost-pandemic worldis confusing many job applicants who want to dress to impress.
“If the last six years has proven anything, it’s that everyone and everything has become slightly more relaxed,” said Christina Adamo, a personal stylist at the Neiman Marcus store in Paramus, New Jersey. “That especially goes for dress codes, in great part because of the transition a lot of companies have had to hybrid andremote work.”
Wearing awell-tailoredsuit is still frequently prescribed when interviewing for executive positions and jobs in fields such as law and finance, stylists and staffing recruiters said. But it’s worth exploring an organization in advance to get a sense of the culture, or asking the hiring manager or recruiter directly about the dress code. Getting it right, or wrong, may impact your performance, especially during a face-to-face meeting.
“If you walk in and you’re already feeling out of place in the atmosphere, your answers just aren’t as good,” said McEwen, 20, who manages a studentcareer closetof donated suits and work attire at her university. “Most of what matters about your interview outfit is that you feel confident about it. It puts you in the mindset that you’re going to succeed.”
One way to scope out an organization’s style vibe is to check its social media accounts or website to see what employees wear. For example, the career section of The Walt Disney Co.’s website features photos of an attorney, a writer and a maintenance technician employed by the company. After learning how employees in your line of work typically dress, prepare to look a little more polished than that for your interview, experts advised.
“If you were to look at a company’s LinkedIn page and they’re using words like ‘We’re fresh, we’re innovative, we’re the new kids on the block, we’re here to shock the industry,’ then you know that the dress code is going to be more casual than if they’re saying ‘We are a traditional historic brand with traditional values,’” said Samantha Harman, a London-based personal stylist and author of “Just Get Dressed,” a personal style guide for women.
If you’re going for a more senior role, think about refreshing your style so you don’t look dated, Harman, 37, said. “You don’t want anyone to think that you have a dated skill set because you want to be seen as someone who’s innovative, who’s going to have lots of new ideas.”
Sometimes, even after doing the research, candidates find they’re dressing up more than their interviewers. Molly Tyndale, 22, wore a blouse and suit jacket to an online interview for a business development position after she was told by the company that the dress code was “business professional.” She was surprised when one of her interviewers showed up wearing an athletic T-shirt.
“If I, as the candidate, had joined in a T-shirt, that would almost certainly be an automatic no,” she said. “It’s frustrating.”
A wardrobe can be a personal branding tool for your career, Harman said. Hiring managers for senior positions are increasingly asking, “Does this person look like somebody we can send out if there’s a crisis and we need somebody to talk to the media? Or does this person look like they could host our next internal conference? Do they look like we could put them on a stage?” she said.
To convey quiet confidence as a publicist in Los Angeles, Dylan Thomas Cotter wears a dark blue tailored suit to job interviews or meetings where he’s trying to land a new client. In public relations, “if something goes south, we need to immediately look like we’re capable to handle that,” Cotter, 43, said. “But also, when we make our first impression on behalf of our clients, we can make or break their business if we’re not good at what we do.”
If you want to be perceived as a leader, think about watching fall fashion shows to see what colors will likely be trendy in the spring, and wear those colors before that season, Harman suggested. Browsing through Vogue magazine can show you what colors or silhouettes are popping. “Always look at shoes and bags, because they have interesting updates that could look quite cool,” she said.
People on a budget can explore thrift stores or community organizations that offer donated career clothing.
While formality levels vary from one workplace to the next, some interview-dressing guidelines almost always are worth following.
“Make sure everything is nice and clean and presentable,” to convey that you’re taking the opportunity seriously, said Jamie Close, a Charleston, South Carolina-based corporate recruiter at HireQuest, a national staffing and recruiting firm. “Then you’ll feel more confident about yourself as well because you’re not worried about ill-fitting clothes.”
Don’t buy something new and wear it for the first time to an interview, Close advised. “Make sure you’ve worn it somewhere before so you know how it feels when you’re sitting down or standing up and you’re not constantly fidgeting with your clothes,” she said.
If you’re interviewing for a job in the skilled trades, “wear what you wear to work, but wear that nice, clean version,” Close suggested. “Clean boots, a nice collared shirt, ready to work. But not like you just walked off of a work site.”
Dress for a virtual interview the same way you would for an in-person meeting, experts said. Even if the camera will only show your head and torso, Harman suggests wearing shoes because they can signal to your brain to behave in a different way.
For virtual interviews, wearing solid colors is a good choice, because those tend to look better on camera than busy patterns, Adamo said.
“You want to show up as the best version of yourself and that includes dressing the part,” Adamo said. “While many would suggest ‘waist up’ dressing since your top half is doing most of the work, I recommend treating it as if you were going in person. It helps put you in the right headspace, and feeling confident in what you’re wearing is the most important part.”

item.title: 韩国卫星捕捉到 SpaceX 火箭月球坠毁前后的景象
item.description:
佛罗里达州卡纳维拉尔角（美联社）——一颗韩国卫星捕捉到了由 SpaceX 流浪火箭造成的月球新坠毁场景的第一张照片。
周三，猎鹰 9 号上级不慎坠入月球后不久，韩国航空宇宙研究所的 Danuri 航天器飞越了撞击地点。达努里进行了多次飞行，从月球轨道上拍摄了照片，航天局周四发布了这些照片。
美国宇航局和韩国航空航天研究所提供的这组图像显示了 2015 年 10 月 1 日（左）和 2026 年 8 月 5 日（星期三）SpaceX 火箭部分与月球相撞之前（左）和右（右）之后的月球表面区域。（美国宇航局、韩国航空航天研究所，美联社）
火箭撞击处的地形明显更暗，并形成了一个陨石坑，灰尘和岩石到处飞扬。韩国太空官员表示，达努里在枪击前后聚集。
美国宇航局预计其月球勘测轨道飞行器将于下周飞越坠机地点以查看后果。
埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 的 SpaceX 于 2022 年从卡纳维拉尔角发射了 Danuri。
该公司去年还向月球发射了一对私人月球着陆器。据 SpaceX 称，此次发射的上级火箭本周以 5,400 英里/小时（8,700 公里/小时）的速度撞向月球，由于太阳活动和重力而发生意外碰撞。
美联社健康与科学部得到霍华德休斯医学院科学教育部和罗伯特伍德约翰逊基金会的支持。美联社对所有内容全权负责。
